subtopicTitle: Optimal staging — equal mass ratios (for same Isp)

cards.front: Define mass ratio R for a rocket stage.
cards.back: R = m_initial / m_final, where m_final is the mass after propellant is expended (payload + structure + upper stages).

cards.front: State the optimality condition for staging when all stages have identical Isp.
cards.back: For fixed total Δv and number of stages n, total initial mass is minimized when every stage has the identical mass ratio R.

cards.front: Write the expression for total Δv of an n-stage rocket with equal mass ratios R and identical exhaust velocity v_e.
Solve for the optimal common mass ratio R given Δv_total, n stages, and v_e.
Why does equal mass ratio minimize gross mass (intuitive argument)?
cards.back: Because Δv is linear in ln(R) while vehicle mass grows exponentially with R; any imbalance in the ln(R) contributions increases the product of the stage mass multipliers.

cards.front: Derive the condition d(m0)/dR_i = 0 that shows all R_i must be equal (same v_e).
cards.back: Let m0 = m_pay * ∏(R_k / σ_k). With identical v_e, Lagrange multiplier or direct differentiation of ln(m0) subject to ∑ v_e ln(R_k) = Δv yields R_1 = R_2 = … = R_n.

cards.front: How does the presence of non-zero structural mass fraction ε affect the equal-R result?
cards.back: The equal-mass-ratio rule remains exactly optimal only when ε = 0. With ε > 0 the optimum shifts slightly toward lower R on lower stages; the equal-R solution is still a very good first approximation.

cards.front: For a 3-stage vehicle needing 9 km/s with v_e = 3 km/s, compute the optimal R.
